title: Is the Sudoku Board Valid?

concept.title: One set for every row, column and box
body: A sudoku board is valid when no digit repeats in any **row**, any **column** or any of the nine **3 by 3 boxes**. Walk over all filled cells and record, for each cell, three facts in a set: "digit `d` is in row `i`", "digit `d` is in column `j`" and "digit `d` is in box `(i // 3, j // 3)`". If one of the three facts is already in the set, a rule is broken.
The board only has to be valid so far: it does not have to be solvable. The box of a cell is found by integer division of its row and column by 3.

statement: A partially filled sudoku board has 9 lines of 9 characters: a digit from 1 to 9 or a dot for an empty cell. Print `yes` if no digit occurs twice in any row, any column or any of the nine 3 by 3 boxes, otherwise print `no`. You do not have to check that the board can be solved.
constraints: Each character is a digit from 1 to 9 or a dot.
hints: Use a set of facts such as (row, i, digit), (column, j, digit) and (box, bi, bj, digit).
The box of a cell is `(i // 3, j // 3)`.
If a fact is already in the set when a cell is read, the board is invalid.
